A soil-centered field photograph showing a legible moment of material change in earth. A woman with the face-and-hair appearance of the supplied photograph works on an old outdoor clay tennis court just after a rain shower. Her short dark brown chin-length bob and wispy separated fringe retain the visible hair reference. Her dark brown eyes, soft rounded oval face and naturally full lips retain the visible face reference. At the shutter she is pushing a broad cylindrical hand roller over the rain-roughened earthen surface. Both hands grip the same crossbar at waist height, her elbows remain slightly bent, and the two side arms of the handle connect visibly to the roller axle. She leans into one slow step with her boots staggered on firm ground. The cylinder presses the rough damp clods into a continuous smooth strip trailing behind it, while an irregular ridge of loose earth remains immediately ahead of its contact edge. The smooth strip catches soft light differently from the still-lumpy surface. Her attentive sideways glance follows the boundary of the newly flattened clay; parted lips and a loose lock of hair give the practical effort a quiet personal appeal.
